# stable_id|category|genres|premise

wd-p-0777|craft|historical,realist|A typesetter discovers that the corrected version of a proclamation changes who owns the press printing it. The first sheets are already distributed, and either version can be used to accuse the workers of disobedience.

wd-p-0778|route|historical,adventure|A canal boat operator reaches a lock closed by workers demanding overdue wages. Her cargo contains the timber needed to repair the lock's unsafe gate, but delivering it would appear to break the workers' blockade.

wd-p-0779|recordkeeping|historical,mystery|A parish clerk finds a birth entered in a burial register. The mistake protected a family from a tax, but correcting it now would establish the identity of an adult seeking a rightful inheritance.

wd-p-0780|resources|historical,political|A miller is ordered to grind grain for an approaching army. The flour belongs to households whose reserve has already been counted as supplied, and the official requisition would make that accounting fiction real.

wd-p-0781|identity|historical,romance|Two adults correspond through a public letter writer without knowing they use the same intermediary. The writer recognizes their growing attachment but has promised each that their difficulty writing will remain private.

wd-p-0782|proof|historical,mystery|A map engraver finds a harbor added to a plate after official approval. The harbor does exist, but acknowledging it would reveal that a celebrated voyage reached its destination using knowledge borrowed without credit.

wd-p-0783|coordination|historical,adventure|A railway telegraphist receives an instruction to send a train onto a siding already occupied by a work crew. The official code is valid, but the sender used the station's old name for the wrong line.

wd-p-0784|care|historical,family|A laundress recognizes a repaired garment as one her missing daughter made. The customer claims it was purchased secondhand and offers payment to have the distinctive repair removed before returning for it.

wd-p-0785|status|historical,satire|A village orders a grand sign announcing its new market status. The sign painter discovers that the title grants rights only when the sign includes a fee schedule the council wants omitted for elegance.

wd-p-0786|choice|historical,romance|A traveling musician is offered a permanent position that requires changing the instrument associated with a former teacher. The person urging acceptance is also the person who preserved that teacher's unfinished music.

wd-p-0787|craft|historical,mystery|A bookbinder finds that the paper used to reinforce a valuable volume comes from a suppressed petition. Reading the full text requires dismantling the book commissioned to celebrate the official who rejected it.

wd-p-0788|route|historical,adventure|A coach driver knows a flooded ford can be crossed using a nearby private bridge. Its owner will open the gate only to passengers willing to sign a statement about the disputed road's ownership.

wd-p-0789|recordkeeping|historical,political|A census clerk is ordered to count workers where they sleep rather than where their families live. The resulting figures would justify moving public services away from the community supporting those workers.

wd-p-0790|resources|historical,family|A family of weavers receives an order large enough to save the workshop. The specified pattern is one developed by the relative whose contribution the family erased when she left the trade.

wd-p-0791|identity|historical,mystery|A portrait painter recognizes the same sitter in paintings commissioned under two family names. The sitter wants a third portrait that will make the resemblance obvious without requiring an explicit claim.

wd-p-0792|proof|historical,political|A surveyor can prove that a village's common land was enclosed incorrectly. The proof relies on measurements taken by residents whom the court refuses to recognize as qualified witnesses.

wd-p-0793|coordination|historical,adventure|A lighthouse tender receives fuel for a new burner but no instructions for converting the old lamp. The supply ship leaves before the first night, and an arriving vessel expects the brighter light as a navigation signal.

wd-p-0794|care|historical,family|A midwife keeps a private record of unpaid work to remember which families need help. A tax collector mistakes the book for outstanding debts, threatening to convert acts of care into claims against the people she intended to protect.

wd-p-0795|status|historical,satire|A town prepares a ceremonial welcome for a visiting official using borrowed silver. The silver belongs to the person whose petition the official has refused to hear, and returning it would dismantle the impressive display.

wd-p-0796|choice|historical,romance|Two adult apprentices finish training with the same master. The only available workshop can support one trade, and choosing whose work it will house would turn their hoped-for partnership into an employer's hierarchy.

wd-p-0797|craft|historical,political|A shipwright finds that a proposed safety improvement would make existing vessels fail inspection. The harbor depends on those vessels for food, and the owners offer to fund the invention only if its evidence stays unpublished.

wd-p-0798|route|historical,mystery|A postal rider discovers letters delivered through a route officially closed for winter. The route is being maintained by households receiving no payment, and one missing letter would prove who diverted the official allowance.

wd-p-0799|recordkeeping|historical,family|A woman helping settle an estate finds her mother's wages entered as gifts. Correcting the account would establish years of unpaid labor but reduce the inheritance that now supports a younger relative.

wd-p-0800|resources|historical,adventure|A winter caravan reaches a refuge whose fuel was promised to the next travelers. Burning it saves the current party, but the guide knows the next group includes people unable to reach another shelter.

wd-p-0801|identity|historical,political|A schoolteacher is asked to certify pupils under names chosen by an official registry. Several families use different names at home, and signing the certificates would make the official versions the only recognized link to their children's records.

wd-p-0802|proof|historical,mystery|A jeweler finds a repair hidden beneath a newly added hallmark. The repair proves the object predates the workshop claiming it, but the original maker taught the technique to a rival he publicly accused of theft.

wd-p-0803|coordination|historical,adventure|A bell-ringer must warn a valley about a broken embankment using a pattern reserved for fire. The separate flood bell was sold to fund repairs, and residents may run toward the gathering point now under water.

wd-p-0804|care|historical,romance|A person recovering from injury receives lessons in writing from a neighbor. The first letter they can write alone is an application that would take them away from the teacher whose patience made departure possible.

wd-p-0805|status|historical,satire|A village is granted permission to hold a fair under a name nobody uses locally. The printer produces both names, and officials demand the familiar one be removed before recognizing the gathering as lawful.

wd-p-0806|choice|historical,family|A family business is offered a new machine on credit. The person most able to operate it is the apprentice whose training contract forbids independent work, making modernization depend on changing the family's understanding of belonging.

wd-p-0807|craft|historical,mystery|A stained-glass worker restoring a window finds a face painted beneath a donor's portrait. The hidden figure holds the tool needed to identify the workshop omitted from the cathedral's official building record.

wd-p-0808|route|historical,political|A bridge toll collector discovers that the exemption for local residents uses a boundary changed by the bridge's construction. The displaced households must now pay to reach land they still farm on the opposite bank.

wd-p-0809|recordkeeping|historical,mystery|A shipping clerk finds cargo listed as ballast that was carefully insured. The weight matches books removed from a school, and the insurer's signature belongs to its publicly indifferent former patron.

wd-p-0810|resources|historical,family|A family saves coal by sharing one heated room with a neighbor. When the neighbor is offered better housing, the family must decide whether asking her to stay is companionship or a claim on help she never promised indefinitely.

wd-p-0811|identity|historical,romance|Two adults meet during a festival in which clothing marks temporary civic roles. Their later courtship is complicated when one discovers that the authority admired in the other belonged only to a borrowed ceremonial office.

wd-p-0812|proof|historical,political|A court interpreter discovers that a land claim was rejected using a translated place name found nowhere in local speech. Reopening the case requires proving that an earlier respected interpreter chose the wrong landmark.

wd-p-0813|coordination|historical,adventure|A ferry crew must transport a cart carrying a replacement axle for the ferry's own landing crane. The damaged crane cannot unload it, forcing the crew to improvise without losing the mechanism needed for the return trip.

wd-p-0814|care|historical,family|A baker supplies bread anonymously to a household in difficulty. When the household publicly thanks a wealthier neighbor, correcting the mistake would reveal both the gift and the neighbor's refusal to help.

wd-p-0815|status|historical,satire|A town's ceremonial clock is set to flatter a visiting dignitary's arrival. The altered time then governs workers' pay, and the clock keeper is told not to correct it until after the official celebration.

wd-p-0816|choice|historical,romance|A couple plans to leave their town on the first affordable passage. One receives a commission to make an object that will outlast the town itself, turning a temporary delay into the opportunity neither expected to want.

wd-p-0817|craft|historical,adventure|A rope-maker discovers that a rescue order specifies a decorative knot that weakens the line. The ceremonial requirement was copied from a portrait, and refusing it risks losing the contract that would supply a safe replacement.

wd-p-0818|route|historical,mystery|A road inspector finds a milestone moved closer to the town. The shift makes a coach journey appear lawful within a time limit, but the person who moved it was trying to correct a distance wrongly charged to travelers.

wd-p-0819|recordkeeping|historical,political|A clerk records workers' names on a relief list that will also be used to enforce old debts. Separating the lists would preserve access to food while violating the official condition under which aid was funded.

wd-p-0820|resources|historical,family|A fishing family must choose between repairing a boat and replacing a roof before winter. The person offering credit wants the boat pledged as security, although the roof shelters relatives who own a share of it.

wd-p-0821|identity|historical,mystery|A theater dresser recognizes an embroidered mark on a patron's cloak as the laundry code of a long-closed institution. The patron has commissioned a play about that institution under an entirely different account of its residents.

wd-p-0822|proof|historical,political|A printer keeps a faulty proof sheet showing that a censorship order was changed after a book was confiscated. Publishing the evidence would identify the worker who secretly warned the author before the seizure.

wd-p-0823|coordination|historical,adventure|An expedition's interpreter learns that the hired porters agreed to a destination short of the final pass. The leader believes the full journey was paid for, and the supplies cannot be divided without stranding one group.

wd-p-0824|care|historical,romance|A clock repairer continues maintaining the timepiece of someone who has moved away. A new resident begins leaving payment, and their correspondence grows around a routine neither originally intended as an invitation.

wd-p-0825|status|historical,satire|A guild requires proof of independent work before granting permission to work independently. An applicant submits a tool made for the guild's own examiner, who has praised it publicly without asking who made it.

wd-p-0826|choice|historical,family|A family must choose which child will inherit a workshop, but both adult heirs want different work. Their proposed sale would fund both ambitions while ending the craft through which the parent understands the family's place in town.

wd-p-0827|craft|historical,mystery|A bell founder recognizes the alloy of a stolen ceremonial bell in ordinary tools sold locally. Reclaiming the metal would take essential equipment from people who bought it without knowing its origin.

wd-p-0828|route|historical,adventure|A mail coach is diverted through a toll road after a bridge fails. The driver carries an official exemption valid only on the original route, and paying the new fee would use money entrusted for an urgent delivery.

wd-p-0829|recordkeeping|historical,family|A daughter finds that her father's apprenticeship papers list a sponsor he always described as an enemy. The sponsor's descendants now ask the family to return a tool presented as a gift at the end of that apprenticeship.

wd-p-0830|resources|historical,political|A town requisitions empty rooms for displaced families. A boarding-house keeper has left rooms vacant because they are unsafe, but declaring the defects would close the only occupied rooms financing repairs.

wd-p-0831|identity|historical,romance|Two adults meet while cataloging a private collection and discover they are each claiming a different part for their families. Their growing trust depends on acknowledging that cooperation may reduce what either can recover alone.

wd-p-0832|proof|historical,mystery|A paper-maker identifies a letter's date from the watermark but finds that the sheet was stored blank for decades. The apparent old confession may be recent, and the warehouse ledger lists everyone with access to the unused stock.

wd-p-0833|coordination|historical,adventure|A rescue crew can reach a flooded mine through an unused ventilation shaft. The shaft's map uses a local name translated incorrectly on the official plan, sending the second crew toward the wrong hillside.

wd-p-0834|care|historical,family|A relative sends money home under a neighbor's name to avoid reopening a family quarrel. When the neighbor dies, the family plans to honor the wrong benefactor and asks the true sender to contribute to the memorial.

wd-p-0835|status|historical,satire|A public competition requires an entry fee that its prize was intended to help poor entrants overcome. The organizer offers one free place and discovers that selecting its recipient recreates the patronage the competition was meant to replace.

wd-p-0836|choice|historical,romance|An adult offered a teaching post must supply a character reference from someone who disapproved of the relationship that made the work possible. Asking the reference forces both people to revisit an unresolved judgment without making affection an application credential.

wd-p-0837|craft|historical,political|A builder discovers that a public hall's cheapest stone came from dismantled communal steps. Finishing the hall would create a gathering place by making the route to it inaccessible to the residents expected to use it.

wd-p-0838|route|historical,mystery|A canal clerk notices that a vessel's recorded tolls imply it passed through a lock too narrow for its beam. The vessel's cargo was transferred en route at a warehouse absent from the customs account.

wd-p-0839|recordkeeping|historical,family|A family bible contains dates written in two calendar systems. A grandchild correcting them discovers that a long-remembered betrayal was an ordinary delay made suspicious by comparing incompatible dates.

wd-p-0840|resources|historical,adventure|A survey party reaches a pass with enough food only if it follows the planned descent. A newly discovered village can offer shelter but asks the party to carry news along a longer route before winter closes it.

wd-p-0841|identity|historical,political|A registrar is ordered to assign permanent surnames using occupations. A family whose livelihood is changing asks for a name that will not bind its descendants to the work officials assume they must continue doing.

wd-p-0842|proof|historical,mystery|A clock in a courtroom stopped before a disputed agreement was signed. Its repair ledger shows the clock was running correctly that day, but it had been set to the railway's time rather than the town's.

wd-p-0843|coordination|historical,adventure|A sailing crew loses its pilot's chart but retains the list of sounding depths. The depths identify two possible channels, and only one remains safe after the tide turns earlier than the calendar predicts.

wd-p-0844|care|historical,romance|A person offers to read correspondence aloud to a neighbor with failing sight. One letter concerns the reader directly, and continuing faithfully requires revealing a relationship the writer assumed was already known.

wd-p-0845|status|historical,satire|A town rents ceremonial uniforms for a procession but can afford only one rank of insignia. The costume maker proposes identical marks, and officials object that spectators would no longer know whom to applaud first.

wd-p-0846|choice|historical,family|An adult heir is asked to retain a family name as a condition of inheriting a shop. The name attracts customers but also preserves a claim of sole ownership that excluded the relative who taught the heir the trade.

wd-p-0847|craft|historical,mystery|A glassmaker finds bubbles in a window arranged according to a familiar workshop shorthand. The pattern records a warning left by an apprentice whose official report describes the same work as flawless.

wd-p-0848|route|historical,adventure|A guide promises to lead a medical party through a mountain estate. A new owner closes the path, and the guide must decide whether an old verbal permission survives the change without turning the patients into participants in the dispute.

wd-p-0849|recordkeeping|historical,political|A town counts only households with a hearth when distributing winter fuel. Families sharing communal kitchens disappear from the calculation, and the official asked to correct it has already certified the allocation as sufficient.

wd-p-0850|resources|historical,family|A workshop survives by borrowing tools from an estranged relative. When a valuable commission arrives, the owner demands the tools back, offering to sell them only if the family acknowledges why they were lent in the first place.

wd-p-0851|identity|historical,romance|A couple plans a small ceremony using names chosen for their new life. A required witness knows only the names attached to old obligations, and helping them begin again would involve deciding what must honestly be carried forward.
